Priya: Quick follow-up from the residency RFC. I sketched a different compromise: a "handshake token" that encodes short ownership + a small consensus window (50-500ms) to allow local fast-paths without full active/active. Thoughts?

Owen: Walk me through the handshake flow at a high level.

Priya: Client -> regional proxy. Proxy checks escrow owner. If local==owner -> normal commit. If not, proxy attempts a handshake with owner: owner can either issue a short-lived handshake token (valid for X ms) that lets proxy commit locally and later reconcile, or reject and require sync-forward. Handshake token includes epoch and owner-signed HMAC.

Mei: So token grants temporary write permission to non-owner region? That needs strict bounds. What are the safety checks?

Priya: Exactly. Safety: token TTL small (50-500ms depending on tenant SLO). Tokens include `epoch` and `fence_id`. Owner increments epoch on ownership change which invalidates tokens. Proxies must verify signature + epoch before allowing local commit.

Harish: How do we handle DB invariants like uniqueness or monotonic seqs?

Priya: Owner remains authoritative for canonical IDs. Local commits use provisional ids + token-stamped metadata. Reconciler maps provisional -> canonical. For unique constraints we do pre-checks at owner during handshake (owner can return `deny` if conflict likely). If owner returns `allow-with-warning`, proxy can choose to enqueue instead.

Owen: What about p99 spikes? Handshake adds an extra roundtrip. How's this better than sync-forward?

Mei: Because handshake is only attempted once per token TTL and proxies cache the token, so subsequent requests in TTL fast-path. Also handshake window is tunable per-tenant; for high-throughput tenants we can prefer eventual-mode (no handshake).

Priya: Right. Modes per-tenant: owner-only, handshake-sync, eventual. Control-plane stores mode and per-tenant handshake TTL. Proxies cache both.

Harish: Failure modes? If owner accepts handshake but then crashes before canonicalizing?

Priya: Reconcile handles that: provisional records older than reconciliation threshold get rolled back or re-applied depending on owner state. We keep idempotent reconcile jobs and compensating ops for conflicts. Also, tokens are issued only if owner believes it can process backlog within a bounded window.

Owen: Can you show a minimal proxy pseudo-flow?

Priya: Sure:
```
owner = checkEscrow(tenant)
if owner == local -> commitLocal()
else if manifest.mode == "handshake-sync" {
  token = cachedToken(tenant)
  if token.valid() && verify(token) { commitProvisional(token); return 200 }
  resp = callOwnerHandshake(timeout=150ms)
  if resp.allow { cacheToken(resp.token); commitProvisional(resp.token); return 200 }
  if manifest.allow_eventual { enqueueProvisional(); return 202 }
  return 409
}
else if manifest.mode == "eventual" { enqueueProvisional(); return 202 }
else return 403
```

Mei: Telemetry: tag requests with `residency.decision` = {local-owner, handshake-provisional, forwarded, queued, rejected} and track `residency.handshake_latency_ms`. Also surface reconcile conflict_rate by tenant.

Harish: Security: HMAC-signed tokens stored in escrow KV and optionally encrypted when tenant has PII flag. All cross-region handshake calls produce audit events.

ops-bot: small sim uploaded -> https://ci.redwood/sims/handshake-token/3789123456 (10k reqs/tenant, 40% writes). With a 60% token hit-rate, measured app-level p95 on handshake-sync tenants dropped ~30%.

deploy-bot: artifacts + pre-canary checklist posted -> https://ci.redwood/canaries/handshake-token/3789123456

Priya: Implementation owners suggested: escrow token API + signing (Mei / eng-runtime), proxy handshake + token cache (Owen / eng-platform), reconcile worker + compensators (Harish / eng-sre), control-plane per-tenant config (product/infra).

Owen: I'll take proxy changes.

Mei: I'll own escrow token signing and epoching.

Harish: Reconciler owner here. I'll add canary gating metrics.

Priya: Great. I'll draft RFC addendum with sequence diagrams, token proto, and canary plan. Meeting to review tomorrow. :rocket:
